statement: For matrices A, B of compatible shape and scalar c, the transpose satisfies: (A^T)^T = A; (A+B)^T = A^T + B^T; (cA)^T = c(A^T); (AB)^T = B^T A^T. All four follow directly from the entrywise definition [A^T]_ij = [A]_ji.

symbols.meaning: matrices (A is m x n, B conformable for the operation in question)

steps.text: Start from the defining entrywise relation of the transpose: [A^T]_ij = [A]_ji.
Involution: apply the definition twice, [(A^T)^T]_ij = [A^T]_ji = [A]_ij for every i,j, so (A^T)^T = A.
Additivity: [(A+B)^T]_ij = [A+B]_ji = [A]_ji + [B]_ji = [A^T]_ij + [B^T]_ij for every i,j, so (A+B)^T = A^T + B^T.
Scalar homogeneity: [(cA)^T]_ij = [cA]_ji = c[A]_ji = c[A^T]_ij for every i,j, so (cA)^T = c(A^T). Together with additivity this makes transposition a linear map on the space of m x n matrices.

Product reversal: expand the (i,j) entry of AB using the definition of matrix multiplication, [(AB)^T]_ij = [AB]_ji = sum_k [A]_jk [B]_ki. Rewrite each factor via the transpose definition, [A]_jk = [A^T]_kj and [B]_ki = [B^T]_ik, giving sum_k [B^T]_ik [A^T]_kj = [B^T A^T]_ij for every i,j. Hence (AB)^T = B^T A^T; by induction this extends to (A_1 A_2 ... A_k)^T = A_k^T ... A_2^T A_1^T.

assumptions.assumption: Entries lie in a field where scalar multiplication commutes (e.g. real or complex numbers), so [A]_jk[B]_ki can be reordered freely inside the sum used in step 5.
assumptions.breaks_when: entries are drawn from a noncommutative ring, where the product-reversal law can fail or require a different convention

assumptions.assumption: Matrix shapes are conformable for the operation being transposed (same m x n for the sum; A is m x n and B is n x p for the product).
assumptions.breaks_when: shapes are mismatched, making the operation itself undefined before transposition is even considered

failure_modes.mode: Applying (AB)^T = B^T A^T without reversing order
failure_modes.signature: computed transpose of a product does not equal the product of transposes in original order
failure_modes.cause: forgetting that transposition, like taking an inverse, reverses composition order

failure_modes.mode: Confusing plain transpose with conjugate transpose
failure_modes.signature: identities appear to fail for complex matrices, e.g. A^T A is not positive-semidefinite
failure_modes.cause: the source's real-entry claim (A^T A positive-semidefinite) and the Hermitian/unitary definitions require the conjugate transpose, not the plain transpose, once entries are complex
